tasks.title: Correct redirect-bearing PWA shell responses and recover existing caches
tasks.body:
Goal:
- Remove redirect-bearing offline-shell responses from application navigation and provide a data-preserving update path for existing iOS Safari and installed PWA clients.

Current behavior:
- The owner supplied two iPhone screenshots of habitica-companion.pages.dev failing to open with "Response served by service worker has redirections". Chrome reportedly works; the Chrome platform, iOS version, failing route and device cache state are unspecified.
- service-worker.published.js precaches index.html through Cache.addAll using default-follow Requests and returns the cached Response directly for allowlisted navigation. No redirected-response guard or migration exists. The development worker has no offline fetch handler.
- tests/Functions/pwa.test.mjs returns plain mock objects for cache and network replies. Existing checks cover routes and cache inclusion but omit redirect metadata, response-type constraints, update activation and existing-cache recovery.
- Cloudflare Pages documents HTML URL canonicalization. The Fetch Standard rejects a service-worker response carrying multiple response URLs when the original request redirect mode differs from follow. The repository path therefore supplies a concrete defect candidate; the exact deployed response chain and affected device controller remain unverified. Research and official sources reside in skill-tree/history/processing/ios-startup-2026-10-30/research.md.

Desired behavior:
- Fresh installation, controlled online navigation, prepared offline navigation and relaunch serve a valid same-origin public application shell without incompatible redirect history.
- An existing redirected shell cache can recover after the fixed worker activates, including a worker-only update with an unchanged asset-manifest version. Recovery preserves IndexedDB, credentials, Notes, task journals, original receipts and push subscriptions.
- A refused or failed cache repair remains recoverable through a bounded online path and preserves explicit offline failure. The worker never substitutes a private, foreign, opaque or error document for the public shell.

Touch:
- src/Habitica.WebApp/wwwroot/service-worker.published.js
- tests/Functions/pwa.test.mjs
- skill-tree/documents/pwa-installation.md
- skill-tree/documents/deploy-cloudflare-pages.md
- skill-tree/documents/testing.md
- skill-tree/documents/technical.md and skill-tree/documents/features.md for changed worker/cache behavior

Discovery allowance:
- Inspect js/pwa.js, index.html, manifest.webmanifest, Habitica.WebApp.csproj, build.sh and published service-worker-assets.js to verify worker registration, release packaging, integrity and cache identity. Change registration or a bounded local browser fixture only when necessary for update recovery.
- Inspect public deployment headers and asset identities without credentials when transport permits; record unavailable observations explicitly.

Out of scope:
- Habitica API calls, gameplay, account enrollment, push permission or delivery, credential-policy changes, IndexedDB migration, global site-data clearing, package upgrades, publication and unrelated UI changes.
- Claiming the production iPhone incident closed from synthetic, desktop WebKit, desktop Safari or deployment evidence alone.

Implementation constraints:
- Keep the existing app-route allowlist, sensitive/unknown/foreign network-only behavior, non-GET bypass, manifest identity and same-build asset integrity. Restrict any response reconstruction or repair to validated public shell content; do not launder foreign redirects or weaken integrity checks.
- Keep Blazor shell/assets coherent during install, failed install and activation. Do not force skipWaiting or claim mixed-version clients without evidence of a safe transition.
- Recover installed clients without requiring application UI to run first. Limit cache deletion to application-owned public build caches; do not make full storage erasure the normal workaround.
- Each external observation and browser fixture has a hard deadline and cleanup. Synthetic browser origins contain no real account state and deny outbound service calls.

Questions and required clarifications:
- [Resolved - owner request] Treat the reported startup blocker as critical with priority107, above the inspected queue maximum106.
- [Resolved - repository evidence] Local source repair and reproducible redirect/update qualification need no product decision or real credentials. Publication and physical-device operation require separately selected scope.
- [Resolved - qualification boundary] Missing iOS/Safari version, exact route and current worker/cache identity prevent production incident closure. Record the missing observations under the existing physical-device release gate T-d76d2a9a-1318-4e63-9bb4-73f620b108cc; the broad release gate is context rather than an implementation prerequisite.

Validation:
- Extend the Node worker harness with actual Response-compatible redirect/type/body/header semantics or an explicitly faithful model. Reproduce a followed same-origin index.html redirect and prove the old worker violates navigation response requirements before checking the fixed worker.
- Cover fresh install, direct root and nested app routes with query strings, normal and redirected cached shells, missing cache, unavailable network, invalid/foreign responses, incomplete installation and the existing-to-fixed worker transition with unchanged manifest identity.
- Retain current app-route, sensitive/unknown/foreign/non-GET, registration refusal, public asset filtering and push worker regressions. Run the relevant Functions checks after the frontend Release build described in build-and-release.md; inspect the emitted worker and assets rather than using development mode as acceptance.
- Use an isolated loopback host reproducing Pages HTML canonicalization for an actual service-worker browser lifecycle check. Exercise available Chromium and WebKit engines; record unavailable engine evidence and do not substitute Node mocks for a real browser observation. Seed a failing old-worker control and preserve synthetic data canaries across recovery.
- If visible UI or recovery copy changes, qualify each changed route in readable light and obsidian-glow schemes, phone/desktop widths, normal/enlarged text, focus, primary actions, disabled controls, geometry and contrast under the existing UI rules.

Acceptance:
- A retained pre-fix control demonstrates the redirected cached-shell defect; fixed-worker controls supply navigation-compatible shell responses without losing body, required headers or asset integrity.
- Fresh and existing-cache browser controls load allowlisted app routes online and after offline preparation, preserve non-shell routing boundaries and avoid an update/reload loop.
- A worker-only update recovers an already redirected cached shell while synthetic durable-data and subscription canaries remain unchanged. Failed repair/install cannot activate a partial new build or destroy the working prior cache.
- Published frontend packaging and relevant synthetic/browser checks pass with exact source/artifact identities, named engine versions and explicit limitations. Required browser evidence unavailable in the execution environment prevents local acceptance until the missing check is supplied.
- Report local repair acceptance separately from production publication and affected-iPhone validation. Retain both original screenshots and the missing device/build observations; local acceptance does not close the physical incident.

Documentation updates:
- Explain the actual worker registration, cache response handling, safe update lifecycle and recovery procedure in pwa-installation.md and deploy-cloudflare-pages.md. Replace the inspected deployment paragraphs claiming no worker registration and blanket site-data clearing; keep unrelated release history intact.
- Record redirect/update regression commands and bounded browser/device evidence in testing.md, plus changed current worker ownership in technical.md/features.md. Preserve physical iPhone gates explicitly.

Risks:
- Existing clients can remain controlled by an older waiting worker; a successful build or deployment does not prove update activation. Cache identity can remain unchanged during a worker-only patch.
- An overbroad response rewrite can admit foreign or private content, lose integrity/header semantics or mix Blazor asset versions. Global cache/storage deletion can destroy unrelated local records.
- Public deployment probes are unavailable in the processing environment; the source-level mechanism is an evidence-backed hypothesis for the screenshots rather than a reproduced device diagnosis.
